# api-permission-precheck API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/documentation.cjs. Do not edit. -->

Token-free delegated-scope diagnostics and configuration normalization.

These helpers read supplied values without React context or token acquisition.
Decoded claims and available scopes are diagnostic evidence; the target API
still enforces authorization. No signature or issuer verification is performed.

## SPFX\_GRAPH\_APP\_ID

Microsoft Graph application audience accepted alongside its resource endpoint by normalized Graph requirements.

### Imports

```ts
import { SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Use when

- You compare a decoded Graph token audience with its well-known application identifier.

### Examples

```ts
import { SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID, SPFxJwtPayload } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const payload: SPFxJwtPayload = { aud: SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID, scp: 'User.Read' };
```

## SPFxApiPermissionCheckResult

Detailed precheck outcome extending `SPFxApiPermissionSummary` with observed delegated scopes, audience and tenant metadata. Raw access tokens are never included; these claims are diagnostic and unverified.

### Imports (4)

```ts
import type { SPFxApiPermissionCheckResult } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import type { SPFxApiPermissionCheckResult } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Examples (4)

```ts
import { SPFxApiPermissionCheckResult, evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement, normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const [requirement] = normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements({ graph: ['User.Read'] });
const result: SPFxApiPermissionCheckResult = evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement(requirement, { scp: 'User.Read' });
```

## SPFxApiPermissionCheckStatus

Outcome of one delegated-scope precheck. `available` means the decoded token contains an accepted scope; other values describe configuration, token or acquisition failures. This is diagnostic evidence, not proof that an API operation will succeed.

### Imports (5)

```ts
import type { SPFxApiPermissionCheckStatus } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import type { SPFxApiPermissionCheckStatus } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

`missingScope` has no exact acceptable delegated scope. Acquisition may report
`consentRequired`, `interactionRequired`, `claimsChallenge`,
`conditionalAccessBlocked`, `accessRestricted` (assignment restriction), or
`resourceMisconfigured` (unresolved resource). These are heuristic diagnoses.
`tokenProviderUnavailable` is the hook's inability to obtain its provider.

`audienceMismatch` has no accepted token audience; `unsupportedToken` has no
decodable object payload. `unsupportedPermissionKind` means an unsupported
requirement kind or app roles without delegated scopes. `tokenExpired` also
covers not-yet-valid numeric nbf claims. `invalidRequirement` has incomplete
identity/resource/scope/kind metadata. `transientFailure` covers network,
throttling or temporary acquisition failure; `timeout` reports acquisition
timeout and `unknown` means no more specific diagnostic was determined.

### Examples (5)

```ts
import { SPFxApiPermissionCheckStatus } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const status: SPFxApiPermissionCheckStatus = 'missingScope';
```

### Type (5)

```ts
type SPFxApiPermissionCheckStatus = | 'available'
  | 'missingScope'
  | 'consentRequired'
  | 'interactionRequired'
  | 'claimsChallenge'
  | 'conditionalAccessBlocked'
  | 'accessRestricted'
  | 'resourceMisconfigured'
  | 'tokenProviderUnavailable'

  | 'unsupportedToken'

  | 'unknown'
```

## SPFxApiPermissionConfigurationState

Aggregate UI state: `idle` has no results, `checking` has pending work, `ready` has every required scope, `actionRequired` has remediable required failures, and `cannotDetermine` has unresolved required results.

## SPFxApiPermissionPrecheckConfig

Inputs normalized into delegated-scope requirements, in Graph, custom API, then explicit-requirement order. Duplicate endpoint/scope pairs keep the first entry. Omitted arrays contribute no requirements; normalization performs no token request.

## SPFxApiPermissionPrecheckMode

Token acquisition policy used by the React precheck hook. `passive` cancels supported popup/redirect events; `interactiveAllowed` permits interaction. The standalone service does not apply this policy. Neither mode grants permissions or bypasses consent.

## SPFxApiPermissionSeverity

Presentation severity: available is ok; unknown, transientFailure and timeout are unknown regardless of requiredness; all other unavailable statuses are error for required requirements and warning for optional ones. This differs from aggregate readiness buckets.

## SPFxApiPermissionSummary

Token-free display metadata for a checked requirement, including diagnostic status and administrator remediation. Consumers should branch on `status`, rather than infer success from a message or severity.

### Imports (12)

```ts
import type { SPFxApiPermissionSummary } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import type { SPFxApiPermissionSummary } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Examples (12)

```ts
import { SPFxApiPermissionSummary, evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement, normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const [requirement] = normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements({ graph: ['User.Read'] });
const summary: SPFxApiPermissionSummary = evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement(requirement, { scp: 'User.Read' });
```

```

## classifySPFxApiPermissionError

Classifies a token-acquisition error using message/code heuristics into consent, claims, Conditional Access, interaction, assignment, resource, timeout, transient or unknown outcomes. Classification is diagnostic and does not retry or grant access.

```

- You translate an acquisition failure into token-free remediation/status metadata.

### Examples (18)

```ts
import { classifySPFxApiPermissionError, normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const [requirement] = normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements({ graph: ['User.Read'] });
const result = classifySPFxApiPermissionError(requirement, new Error('AADSTS65001: consent required'));
```

## decodeSPFxJwtPayload

Decodes only the JSON payload of a JWT-shaped string. Malformed/nonobject payloads return undefined; signature, issuer and claim types are not validated. Requires globalThis.atob for payload decoding; unavailable decoding support also returns undefined. Do not log raw tokens or treat decoded claims as verified identity.

```ts
import { decodeSPFxJwtPayload } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

```

### Use when (7)

- You inspect token claims locally for diagnostics without exposing the raw token in results.

### Avoid when

- You need authenticated identity or authorization: payload decoding does not verify the signature, issuer or claim types.

### Examples (20)

```ts
import { decodeSPFxJwtPayload } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const payload = decodeSPFxJwtPayload('header.eyJzY3AiOiJVc2VyLlJlYWQifQ.signature');
```

## evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement

Evaluates a requirement against decoded claims without I/O or signature verification. Checks metadata, token dates, optional audience policy and exact case-sensitive delegated scopes (including explicitly accepted alternatives). App-only roles are unsupported. An available result does not prove an API request will succeed.

### Imports (21)

```ts
import { evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Use when (8)

- You already have decoded claims and need a case-sensitive delegated-scope diagnostic.

### Avoid when (2)

- You need server authorization or app-role permission checks; this evaluates delegated scope evidence only.

### Examples (21)

```ts
import { SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID, evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement, normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const [requirement] = normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements({ graph: ['User.Read'] });
const result = evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement(requirement, { aud: SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID, scp: 'User.Read' });
```

### Signatures (5)

```ts
(requirement: SPFxApiPermissionRequirement, payload: SPFxJwtPayload | undefined, options?: { readonly validateAudience?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined): SPFxApiPermissionCheckResult
```

#### Parameters (5)

- `requirement`: Normalized delegated-scope requirement.
- `payload`: Decoded claims; undefined produces `unsupportedToken`.
- `options`: Omitted enables audience validation; validateAudience false skips it. Missing/empty expected audiences skip comparison in either case.

#### Returns (5)

Detailed diagnostic result without a raw token.

Evaluation compares every string entry in an audience array, even though this display field shows only its first entry. ## extractSPFxDelegatedScopes

Extracts whitespace-trimmed scopes from a string `scp` claim. Ignores app roles and returns an empty array for absent/nonstring claims; duplicate scopes are retained.

### Imports (22)

```ts
import { extractSPFxDelegatedScopes } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { extractSPFxDelegatedScopes } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Use when (9)

- You need delegated scp entries from an already decoded payload for diagnostic comparison.

### Examples (22)

```ts
import { extractSPFxDelegatedScopes } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const scopes = extractSPFxDelegatedScopes({ scp: 'User.Read Mail.Read' });
```

### Signatures (6)

```ts
(payload: SPFxJwtPayload): readonly string[]
```

#### Parameters (6)

- `payload`: Decoded, unverified JWT claims. Scopes split on literal spaces; tabs are trimmed only at each resulting entry boundary.

#### Returns (6)

Delegated scope names in their original case and order.

## normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements

Normalizes configured Graph, custom API and explicit requirements without I/O. Trims configured scope names; Graph and custom scopes default to required. Deduplicates exact endpoint/scope pairs, keeping the first entry; explicit requirements are otherwise preserved.

### Imports (23)

```ts
import { normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Use when (10)

- You combine Graph and custom API scope configuration into ordered, deduplicated diagnostic requirements.

### Examples (23)

#### Basic usage

```ts
import { normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const [requirement] = normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements({ graph: ['User.Read'] });
```

#### Compare illustrative Graph and Orders API requirements

```ts
import {
  evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement,
  normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements,
  summarizeSPFxApiPermissionResults,
  SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID,
  type SPFxApiPermissionPrecheckConfig,
  type SPFxJwtPayload,
} from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const config: SPFxApiPermissionPrecheckConfig = {
  graph: [
    'Sites.Read.All',
    { scope: 'User.Read', required: false, label: 'Profile access' },
  ],
  customApis: [{
    id: 'orders',
    name: 'Orders API',
    resource: 'api://11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111',
    packageResource: 'Orders API',
    scopes: [{ scope: 'Orders.Read', satisfies: ['Orders.ReadWrite'] }],
    expectedAudiences: ['11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111'],
  }],
};

const requirements = normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements(config);
// Illustrative decoded claims only; use the hook/service for real tokens.
const graphPayload: SPFxJwtPayload = {
  aud: SPFX_GRAPH_APP_ID,
  scp: 'Sites.Read.All User.Read',
};
const graphResults = requirements
  .filter(requirement => requirement.id.startsWith('graph:'))
  .map(requirement =>
    evaluateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement(requirement, graphPayload)
  );
const graphSummary = summarizeSPFxApiPermissionResults(graphResults);
// Both Graph requirements are available: configurationState === 'ready'.
// Custom API requirements need their own resource token and are not checked here.
```

### Signatures (7)

```ts
(config: SPFxApiPermissionPrecheckConfig): readonly SPFxApiPermissionRequirement[]
```

#### Parameters (7)

- `config`: Configuration; omitted arrays contribute no requirements.

#### Returns (7)

Ordered, deduplicated requirements; an empty configuration returns an empty array.

## summarizeSPFxApiPermissionResults

Groups available results, required actionable failures, optional failures and unresolved required outcomes. `isConfigured` checks only required results, so an empty set returns true even though its configuration state is `idle`. A checking flag overrides the aggregate state.

Required missingScope, consentRequired, interactionRequired, claimsChallenge,
conditionalAccessBlocked and accessRestricted results enter missing. Other
unavailable required results enter unknown; unavailable optional results enter
warnings regardless of severity. State precedence is checking, empty idle,
actionable missing, all-required available, then cannotDetermine.

### Imports (24)

```ts
import { summarizeSPFxApiPermissionResults } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { summarizeSPFxApiPermissionResults } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Use when (11)

- You render readiness and actionable/optional/unknown buckets from completed prechecks.

### Examples (24)

```ts
import { summarizeSPFxApiPermissionResults } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const summary = summarizeSPFxApiPermissionResults([]);
// summary.configurationState === 'idle'; summary.isConfigured === true
```

```ts
(results: readonly SPFxApiPermissionCheckResult[], isChecking?: boolean | undefined): { readonly configurationState: SPFxApiPermissionConfigurationState; readonly isConfigured: boolean; readonly available: readonly SPFxApiPermissionSummary[]; readonly missing: readonly SPFxApiPermissionSummary[]; readonly warnings: readonly SPFxApiPermissionSummary[]; readonly unknown: readonly SPFxApiPermissionSummary[]; }
```

#### Parameters (8)

- `results`: Completed requirement results.
- `isChecking`: Whether work is still pending; omitted means false.

Aggregate state and token-free UI buckets.

## validateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement

Checks required metadata for a delegated-scope requirement without acquiring a token. Unsupported kinds return `unsupportedPermissionKind`; missing or blank required fields return `invalidRequirement`.

### Imports (25)

```ts
import { validateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { validateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Use when (12)

- You reject incomplete delegated-scope metadata before requesting a token.

### Examples (25)

```ts
import { normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements, validateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const [requirement] = normalizeSPFxApiPermissionRequirements({ graph: ['User.Read'] });
const issue = validateSPFxApiPermissionRequirement(requirement);
```
